title: Maple Junction Moon-Milk Diner Postcard
tests: World That Never Was slot: clearly fictional alternate local-history postcard, period tactile detail, natural readable artifact text, no claim of being real.
prompt:

The finished image should look like a photographed vintage postcard laid on a sign-shop counter, not a modern graphic mockup: aged linen-card texture, softly faded inks, worn corners, slight paper curl, tiny halftone dots, and believable period printing imperfections. The postcard illustration shows a humid summer dusk roadside diner with chrome trim, warm counter lights in the windows, a crescent-shaped neon milk-bottle sign glowing pale blue-white above the roof, hand-painted souvenir racks near the entrance, and a few parked 1950s cars catching reflections from wet pavement. Include small readable fictional place text such as "Maple Junction Moon-Milk Diner" and "Route 6, Pennsylvania" as period postcard lettering, but avoid dense paragraphs and avoid implying this is real. Add inspectable physical details around the card: an old diner matchbook, a pencil, a small stack of color swatches, and dust in raking light. Nostalgic, tactile, richly detailed, plausible alternate local-history artifact, photographed documentary style.
